## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
# Loading libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(skimr)
library(ggplot2)
library(viridis)
library(snakecase)
library(kableExtra)
library(gt)
library(knitr)

#Loading the dataset
opal <- read_csv("~/Desktop/all-modes-dec-2023.csv")
theme_set(theme_minimal())

#Opal trips from 2019 to 2023 sub dataset
opal_2019_2023 <- opal %>%
# Separating Year and Month into 2 different columns for easy reading
 separate(Year_Month, into = c( "Year", "Month"), sep = "-") %>%
clean_names() %>%
  
#Renaming columns
  rename(
    travel_type = travel_mode,
    opal_card = card_type,
    total_trips = trip
  ) %>%
  
  #Converting Year as Numeric and month as a factor
  mutate(
    year = as.numeric(year),
# Abbreviating months    
    month = factor(month.abb[as.numeric(month)], levels = month.abb)
  ) %>%
  filter(year >= 2019 & year <= 2023) 


#Catergorising ticket types by demographic
opal_2019_2023_cleaned <- opal_2019_2023 %>%
  mutate(
    # 1. Clean the Travel Types first
    travel_type = case_when(
      str_detect(travel_type, "Bus") ~ "Bus",
      str_detect(travel_type, "Ferry") ~ "Ferry",
      str_detect(travel_type, "Light rail") ~ "Light rail",
      str_detect(travel_type, "Train|Metro") ~ "Rail", 
      TRUE ~ travel_type
    ),
    # 2. Continue the mutate for Card Types
    opal_card = case_when(
      str_detect(opal_card, "Adult") ~ "Adult",
      str_detect(opal_card, "Child|Student|Youth|Concession") ~ "Student",
      str_detect(opal_card, "Senior|Pensioner") ~ "Senior",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    )
  ) %>%
  # 3. The "Big Shrink" (Grouping and Summarising)
  group_by(year, month, travel_type, opal_card) %>%
  summarise(total_trips = sum(total_trips, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
view(opal_2019_2023_cleaned)
```

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}
#Analysing the subdata set
opal_2019_2023_analysis <- opal_2019_2023_cleaned %>%
  group_by(month, travel_type, opal_card) %>%
  summarise(avg_trip = round(mean(total_trips)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  # NEW STEP BELOW:
  group_by(travel_type, opal_card) %>% 
mutate(pct_of_year = round((avg_trip / sum(avg_trip)) * 100))


 opal_2019_2023_analysis %>% 
   arrange(month)
```

```{r}
#Heatmap visualisation
# CHUNK: Visualisation of Peak Demand
ggplot(opal_2019_2023_analysis, aes(x = month, y = travel_type, fill = pct_of_year)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~opal_card, ncol = 2) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "red") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(title = "Sydney Transport Seasonality", 
       fill = "% of Year")
```

```{r}
operational_peaks %>%
  kable(caption = "Top 10 Operational Peaks by Mode and Category", align = "c") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), 
                full_width = F) %>%
  # Row 0 is the header
  row_spec(0, bold = T, color = "white", background = "#002664") %>%
  # Rows 1 to 10 are the data
  row_spec(1:10, background = "white", color = "black")
```
